1  THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioner-accused is before this Court seeking grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., in Crime No.384/2020 of Ramamurthy Police Station, pending in S.C.No.504/2021 on the file of the learned 10th Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Mayohall, Bengaluru City, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 302, 120(B), 201, 498(A), 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC') on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant Sri.Vasudevan G.S.
2.

entities.text: 10th Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Mayohall, Bengaluru City
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard Sri.Rakshith K.S., learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt.K.P.Yashodha, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent-State.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.?"
NC: 2024:KHC:27101

My answer to the above point is in 'negative' for the following:
REASONS 5.
The petitioner being the sole accused is before this Court seeking grant of bail.
He was apprehended on 29.11.2020 and since then he is in judicial custody.
6. The petitioner is the informant who lodged the first information making allegations against one Vijayakumar.
Investigation was undertaken and it was found that this petitioner had caused the death of the deceased and had filed complaint against the said Vijayakumar.
The charge sheet came to be filed for the offences punishable under Sections 302, 120(B), 201, 498(A), 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of IPC against the petitioner.
Accused No.2-Vijayakumar has died during investigation and therefore, the case against him stood abated.
7. CW-3 is the daughter of the deceased and she is an eye witness to the incident.
She is examined before the Trial Court and she has fully supported the case of the prosecution.
There are other eye witnesses to the incident, who have been NC: 2024:KHC:27101 examined by the Trial Court.
But strangely, the petitioner filed an application seeking grant of bail before the Trial Court as well as before this Court repeatedly without there being any change in the circumstances.
8. It is pertinent to note that this is the 7th petition filed by the petitioner seeking grant of bail.
The earlier petitions were dismissed with the consistent findings that there are prima facie cases against the petitioner for having committed the offence and he is not entitled for grant of bail.

He filed Sri Vasudevan vs State Of Karnataka on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169935173/
2 Crl.P.No.3946/2023 again seeking bail which came to be dismissed vide order dated 05.07.2023 specifically referring to the evidence of CW-3 who is examined as prosecution witness and fully supported the case of the prosecution.

entities.text: Sri Vasudevan vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The contention taken by the petitioner that there are contradictions, omissions or improvements in her evidence cannot be accepted as there are no such glaring material contradictions which compel releasing the petitioner on bail.
However, again the petitioner is knocking the doors of this Court for grant of bail which is nothing but misuse of due process of law.

Therefore, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is not entitled to grant of bail as the material witnesses have fully supported the case of the NC: 2024:KHC:27101 prosecution and the Trial Court has not yet completed the examination of other witnesses.

9. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is dismissed.
Office to communicate this order to the Trial Court for information.

Sd/-
